title: Observability weekly - 2026-03-23
content:
Observability team weekly notes (week of 2026-03-23)

Summary:
- Focus this week: tracing ingestion stability, dashboard refresh and pruning, and cost telemetry anomaly investigation for dedupe cache.
- We had one partial degradation on Thursday (tracing ingestion lag) that impacted internal traces only; no customer-facing errors. Root cause related to a rollout of a hotfix to the trace-collector that regressed backpressure handling.

Attendees (standups + weekly sync):
- Ava Chen (owner)
- Miguel Torres
- Priya Patel
- Liam O'Connor
- Rashmi Iyer
- Oncall: Miguel (03/22-03/24)

Daily standup highlights (short):
- Mon 03/23: Miguel - finished collector metrics labels PR; Priya - dashboard pruning plan drafted; Liam - started query performance profiling for p95 latency; Rashmi - cost telemetry spike analysis started.
- Tue 03/24: Miguel - deployed metrics labels PR to staging; saw improved cardinality filtering; Priya - implemented pruning script for old panel variants (WIP); Ava - validated trace schema changes on dev cluster.
- Wed 03/25: Liam - found slow aggregator join on the time-series store (q=top-5); Miguel - rolled back a candidate patch that caused increased GC under load; Rashmi - isolated cost spike to dedupe-cache miss patterns generated by batch job X.
- Thu 03/26: Incident: tracing ingestion lag 09:40-10:15 PDT. Miguel mitigated by pinning collector to previous version; ingestion recovered. Post-mortem in progress.
- Fri 03/27: Priya - dashboards PR merged (prune + read-only defaults); Ava - updated tracing playbook draft; team retro + action-item sync.

Incident (tracing ingestion lag) - brief timeline:
- 09:35: alerts started for internal tracing delayed batches (alert OBS-TRC-LAG).
- 09:40: noticed spike in collector queue length and consumer timeouts.
- 09:45: rolled hotfix for backpressure logic (candidate from previous week) had been auto-promoted to canary; roll forward to rollback initiated.
- 10:05: rolled back to previous stable image; queue drained progressively.
- 10:15: ingestion rates returned to baseline; alert resolved at 10:20 after 1m sustained good rate.
- Root cause hypothesis: under specific 512-concurrency bursts, the new backpressure heuristics dropped the consumer tokens incorrectly, causing a feedback loop; reproducer under load harness.
- Action items: Miguel to finish post-mortem draft (JIRA-OBS-189), add a unit test for token accounting, and add a canary-guard to prevent auto-promotion for that binary until end-to-end test coverage is present.

Metrics & Observations:
- Tracing ingestion: baseline ~12k spans/min, P99 ingest latency increased from 180ms -> 1.1s during incident.
- Dashboard rendering: average refresh time improved 12% after pruning large legacy panels (PR #278).
- Cost telemetry: monthly dedupe-cache spend anomaly (+18% week-over-week) traced to daily batch job that increased unique keys; Rashmi narrowed to a malformed payload from service batch-rewrite which caused high churn.
- Alerts: tuned OBS-TRC-LAG threshold to consider queue growth rate rather than absolute size to reduce noise.

Work items completed this week:
- PR 278: dashboard pruning + read-only defaults merged (Priya).
- Collector metrics labels PR deployed to staging (Miguel).
- Tracing playbook initial draft updated with incident runbook steps (Ava).
- Cost telemetry spike root-cause narrowed to batch-rewrite payload; mitigation has been merged to staging by Rashmi.

Work planned next week:
- Finish tracing post-mortem and link to playbook (Miguel, due 2026-03-30).
- Add token-accounting unit tests and expand load harness scenarios (Liam & Miguel).
- Rollout dashboard pruning to prod with gradual rollout and telemetry gating (Priya).
- Complete cost telemetry mitigation deploy and add synthetic checks to detect dedupe churn (Rashmi).
- Start a small project to add per-tenant cost tagging to telemetry pipeline (spike) - Ava to scope.

Open questions / blockers:
- Need clarity from Platform on whether we can add a canary gating that prevents auto-promotion of images without passing end-to-end tracing harness (Platform ticket opened, CON-OBS-412).
- Query performance profiling: need additional VM capacity to reproduce high-cardinality joins in prod-like environment; raise to infra for quota (Ava).

Action items (owner - due):
- Miguel: finish post-mortem draft and JIRA-OBS-189 updates - due 2026-03-30.
- Liam: implement expanded load scenarios for aggregator profiling - due 2026-04-06.
- Priya: begin canaryed rollout of dashboard pruning to 10% of orgs, monitor render time & error rate - start 2026-03-30.
- Rashmi: deploy dedupe mitigation to prod and add synthetic check - due 2026-03-31.
- Ava: open infra quota request for additional profiling VMs - due 2026-03-27.

Notes / miscellaneous:
- Suggested follow-up: schedule a 60m cross-team sync (Platform + Observability + Release Eng) to discuss safe canary promotion flows. Tentative invite for 2026-03-29.
- Quick wins: add a lightweight dashboard that surfaces collector queue growth rate + backpressure state, and an automated rollback playbook linked to the tracing playbook.
- "Notes to self" (Ava): remember to include a blameless framing paragraph in the incident post-mortem and link to the tracing-playbook early in the doc.

Relevant links & artifacts:
- Post-mortem tracking: JIRA-OBS-189
- Tracing playbook draft: https://confluence.redwood.example/display/OBS/Tracing+Playbook
- Dashboards PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/278
- Collector metrics labels PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/282

Next weekly sync: 2026-03-30 (standup notes will be appended here).

-- end of note --
